title: the tenth guru, the khalsa, the saint-soldier
hook: the tenth Guru, the Khalsa, the saint-soldier
tomorrow: a scripture that is the guru

segments.voice: Yesterday: the five Ks. Your line was reminders you can touch. Today, the Guru they trace back to. Day nineteen.
screen: `THE FIVE KS — REMINDERS YOU CAN TOUCH.` → `DAY 19.`

segments.voice: Nine years old. A father leaving home, knowing he may not come back. He has gone to the capital to stand up for the right of people from another faith to practice theirs, and he doesn't come back. Now the community turns to the boy and tells him: you are the Guru. That's how the tenth Guru's leadership began, in 1675, as Sikh tradition tells it. The boy grew into a poet, a warrior and the founder of the Khalsa.
screen: `NINE YEARS OLD.` → `A FATHER WHO DOESN'T COME BACK.` → `YOU ARE THE GURU.`

segments.voice: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth and last human Guru of the Sikhs. His father was the ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur. Sikh tradition remembers that he went to Delhi on behalf of Hindu Kashmiri pandits who were being pressed to convert, and was executed there by the Mughal authorities. Sikhs honor him as a martyr who gave his life for the freedom of others to worship. That memory shaped his son. Guru Gobind Singh taught that a person of faith should be two things at once. The Sikh phrase is sant sipahi: saint and soldier. Saint, because the inner life comes first: remembrance, humility, the name. Soldier, because when the weak are being crushed, a saint doesn't look away. The kirpan from yesterday comes from exactly this. And the order matters. A soldier with no saint in him is only violence; a saint with no courage may stand by while others suffer. He wrote devotional poetry Sikhs still recite every day, and in 1699 he called the five from day four out of the crowd. He lost his father, and all four of his sons, to the violence of his time, and is still remembered for chardi kala. And near the end of his life he decided there would be no eleventh human Guru.
screen: `THE TENTH AND LAST HUMAN GURU.` · `A FATHER WHO DIED FOR OTHERS' FREEDOM.` · `SANT SIPAHI — SAINT AND SOLDIER.` · `THE SAINT COMES FIRST.`

segments.voice: Let one hand rest open on your lap: that's the saint, quiet, open, remembering. Let the other close into a gentle fist: that's the courage to stand up for someone. Feel both at once. Now think of one person in your life who might need someone to stand up for them, and hold them in mind, with both hands.
Guru Gobind Singh. The tenth Guru, founder of the Khalsa, poet and warrior: the saint-soldier. Nineteenth word.
Your line: sword and saint. The saint comes first, and the courage serves it. Day nineteen.

screen: `DAY 19 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A SCRIPTURE THAT IS THE GURU.`

howItsDone: Sikhs honor Guru Gobind Singh as the tenth Guru and founder of the Khalsa, celebrate his birth each year, recite his compositions in daily prayers, and speak of the ideal of the sant sipahi, the saint-soldier.

pairs: where the great gathering was held

myth: Guru Gobind Singh was only a warrior
he was a poet too; Sikhs recite his writing every day.
his father was executed for defending others' freedom to worship
tradition remembers Guru Tegh Bahadur standing up for Kashmiri pandits.
in the saint-soldier, the soldier comes first
the saint comes first. courage serves the inner life, not the other way round.

fork.setup: you're a person of deep prayer, and you see the weak being crushed. what does the saint-soldier do?
options: pray, and stay out of it.
stand up for them, with the saint first.
fork.reveal: sant sipahi: saint first, then soldier. a saint doesn't look away, and a soldier without the saint is only violence.

original.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: the tenth Guru. Singh means lion, the name taken by Khalsa men.

trapdoor: what it means: the tenth Guru: poet and saint-soldier, who founded the Khalsa and held courage and devotion together.
what a scholar hears: he was born Gobind Rai, and tradition says he took the name Singh at the founding of the Khalsa in 1699. he also ended the line of human Gurus.

notes: Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution is described as Mughal and on behalf of Kashmiri pandits pressed to convert; this is the Sikh tradition's account. Confirm the careful framing ('Sikh tradition remembers').
Loss of all four sons (sahibzade) mentioned in one sentence without detail; confirm tone.
Name change Gobind Rai to Gobind Singh at the Khalsa's founding; confirm.
The 1699 story is told briefly on day 4 and in full on days 84–87; the Guru Granth as Guru is day 20.
